title: Broadband emitter localization and prefabrication two-photon interference from InAs/InP quantum dots monolithically grown on an InGaAsP/InP distributed Bragg reflector
authors: Paweł Mrowiński, Jan Śmigiel, Mikołaj Badura, Beata Ściana, Wojciech Kijaszek, Emilia Zięba-Ostój, Paweł Holewa, Marcin Syperek
abstract: We demonstrate a monolithic telecom C-band single-photon platform based on low-density InAs/InP quantum dots grown on an InGaAsP/InP distributed Bragg reflector, with simulated upward light-extraction efficiency exceeding 10% within the 40 nm spectral band. Enhanced light extraction is crucial for wide-field photoluminescence imaging, enabling approximately 3 nm statistical centroid-localization precision of QD emitters due to improved signal-to-noise ratio. The identified charged exciton emitting at 1549.5 nm exhibits single-photon emission purity up to 94.7%, validated by a raw peak-area integration under pulsed quasi-resonant excitation. Under these conditions, photons emitted sequentially from the unprocessed planar structure reveal a raw two-photon interference visibility of 51% of the photon wave packet within the 2 ns time window and 41% over a 4 ns integration window, all without Purcell enhancement typical for cavity-embedded emitters. Combining broadband extraction, high photon coherence, and emitter preselection on a native III-V wafer, this architecture paves the way for marker-based deterministic fabrication of high-quality monolithic nanophotonic devices.
summary: This paper reports on the creation of a monolithic, telecom C-band single-photon source using InAs/InP quantum dots grown on a DBR structure. Key achievements include demonstrating high single-photon purity and significant two-photon interference visibility without the need for optical cavities. This platform is presented as a crucial step toward deterministic, high-quality nanophotonic quantum devices.
main_problem: Developing a scalable, monolithic solid-state single-photon generator operating in the telecom C-band for quantum photonics applications.
main_result: The authors demonstrated a platform achieving high single-photon purity (up to 94.7%) and measurable two-photon interference visibility (51% in 2 ns) in an unprocessed planar structure.
method: The study combines epitaxial growth techniques (InAs/InP QDs on InGaAsP/InP DBR) with advanced optical characterization, including wide-field photoluminescence imaging and Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is a monolithic structure comprising low-density InAs/InP quantum dots embedded within an InGaAsP/InP Distributed Bragg Reflector (DBR) on a native III-V wafer.
key_observables: Two-photon interference visibility (HOM), single-photon emission purity ($g^{(2)}(0)$), upward light-extraction efficiency, and statistical centroid-localization precision.
important_parameters: Telecom C-band (1549.5 nm), 3 nm localization precision, 51% raw TPI visibility, and $\approx 13\%$ simulated extraction efficiency.
main_assumptions: The coherence measurements are performed on an unprocessed planar structure, which is noted to be a limitation compared to cavity-embedded emitters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the sample layout, AFM/SEM images confirming QD morphology and DBR interfaces, and plots showing the time dependence of the two-photon interference visibility.
paper_structure: The work progresses from structural characterization (AFM/SEM) and optical simulation (DBR efficiency) to demonstrating single-photon quality ($g^{(2)}(0)$) and finally quantifying the two-photon coherence via HOM interference.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the hardware requirements for quantum networking by providing a solid-state, telecom-band source with high coherence and integration potential, which is central to photonic quantum information processing.
